draft.title: Government enterprises
card: A government enterprise is a business owned by a government. It sells goods or services, as other businesses do.
Australia Post is one example. It is owned by the Australian Government and delivers mail and parcels across the country.
A government sets up or keeps an enterprise to make sure a service is provided, such as mail to remote areas that a private firm might not serve.
Many government enterprises also aim to make a profit. The aim of providing the service comes first, and profit is often a second aim.
draft.remember: Government ownership is what makes it a government enterprise. Its first aim is usually to provide a service.

a.q: Which of these is a government enterprise?
opts: A bus service owned and run by a state government
A bus service owned by a family in Orange
A bus service owned by shareholders on the ASX
A bus service run by two friends as partners
a.why: A government enterprise is a business owned by a government, so the state-owned bus service fits. The ASX-listed service is owned by shareholders, so it is a public company even though it provides a public service.
a.clue: Look at who owns the business, not what it does.

b.q: A state government keeps a water delivery business to supply remote towns, even though a private firm would find it unprofitable. Why would the government do this?
opts: To make sure a service is provided to those towns
To avoid ever having to charge customers a fee
To give shareholders a high return on their shares
To make sure the business has unlimited liability
b.why: A government enterprise exists to provide a service the government wants provided, even where private firms would not. Profit may be a second aim, but it is not the main reason here, so a high return for shareholders does not fit.
b.clue: Think about why a private firm would not serve these towns.

a.best: A bus service owned and run by a state government

b.best: To make sure a service is provided to those towns

problems.detail: The stem already gives the answer: it says the business supplies remote towns that a private firm would find unprofitable, so the service-provision option is easy to pick without knowing the idea.
The clue 'Think about why a private firm would not serve these towns' points straight to the intended answer.
The clue 'Look at who owns the business, not what it does' points straight to the only government-owned option, so it gives the answer away.
